Wren and Ranger Kim are writing up their quoll survey for the Alpine Wildlife Journal, which is read by scientists across the country. Every report in the journal is checked by experts before it is printed, and anything chatty is sent back to be rewritten.

Survey of spotted-tailed quolls, Snow Gum Gully
In June, we set twelve motion-sensing cameras along the creek in Snow Gum Gully. The weather was cold, with snow on eleven of the twenty-eight nights. Over four weeks, the cameras recorded sixty-three sightings of spotted-tailed quolls. Most sightings occurred between midnight and four in the morning. Ranger Kim identified each quoll by the pattern of white spots on its back. Two cameras were knocked over, probably by wombats, and had to be reset. On 19 June, we located a den beneath a fallen snow gum. The den contained a female and four young, all of which appeared [totally fine]. The female was [observed] carrying food to the den on three separate nights. No foxes were recorded within two hundred metres of the den. We [recommend] that the gully be closed to campers until the young are old enough to leave the den. A full table of sightings is attached. This survey was funded by the Scaffold Peaks Council.
